cover_sub: Understanding the emergency reserves landscape across the nonprofit sector.

slides.label: Overview
slides.headline: Reserve Funding Crisis in U.S. Nonprofits
slides.body: 48% of nonprofits lack adequate emergency reserves, indicating a critical need for financial stability. Data from IRS 990 filings highlights this issue.

slides.label: General Sector
slides.headline: Operating Reserves in Nonprofits
slides.body: Approximately 40% of nonprofits have fewer than 3 months of operating reserves, underscoring the financial fragility of the sector.

slides.label: Small Organizations
slides.headline: Small Orgs and Financial Reserves
slides.body: Organizations under $500K in revenue are more likely to have lean reserves, often reinvesting directly into programs.

slides.label: Data Source
slides.headline: Public IRS 990 Filings
slides.body: This data is derived from public IRS 990 filings, providing a comprehensive view of financial health across the sector.

slides.label: Leadership Perspective
slides.headline: Financial Stability for Nonprofit Leaders
slides.body: Nonprofit leaders must prioritize building and maintaining emergency reserves to ensure long-term sustainability and program delivery.

slides.label: Funding Role
slides.headline: Role of Funders in Financial Health
slides.body: Funders play a crucial role by supporting nonprofits in building their reserves, ensuring they can weather financial storms and continue their missions.

cta_body:
Support emergency savings.
Prioritize long-term sustainability.
